title: Air India Extends Saudi Flight Cancellations to October 20 as Houthi Attacks Continue
excerpt: Air India pushes its Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah cancellations from October 17 to October 20, while IndiGo and Akasa Air extend their Saudi suspensions to October 24.
body:
• Air India has extended cancellations on all flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 20, 2026, three days beyond its earlier October 17 cutoff.
  • IndiGo has extended its Saudi cancellations until October 24, and Akasa Air has suspended Riyadh flights until October 24 and Jeddah until October 21.
  • Affected Air India passengers are being offered a full refund; check your booking status before leaving for the airport, as dates differ by airline and city.
  • The ICAO Council has condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian airports, and the death toll from the October 10 attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has risen to 13, including an Indian national.

Air India on Friday extended the cancellation of all its flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 20, 2026, citing the evolving security situation in Saudi Arabia after a series of Houthi attacks on civilian airports and aviation infrastructure in the kingdom. The airline had previously cancelled its Saudi services, along with Air India Express, until October 17.

"In view of the evolving situation in Saudi Arabia, all Air India flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah stand cancelled until 20 October 2026," the airline said in a statement posted on X, adding that it was closely monitoring developments to determine when operations could safely resume. Passengers affected by the cancellations are being offered a full refund.

Other Indian Carriers Extend Suspensions Further

Air India is not the carrier looking furthest ahead. IndiGo announced on Thursday that it was extending the cancellation of its flights to Saudi Arabia until October 24, according to ANI's report of the extensions. Akasa Air said on Thursday that it had extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh until October 24 and Jeddah until October 21, citing the prevailing security situation in the Middle East. In its earlier advisory, Akasa offered affected passengers a full refund or the option to reschedule without additional charges.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=CweshgraLH0

"Passengers affected by the cancellations are being offered a full refund."

The staggered dates mean there is no single day on which India-Saudi flying resumes. A passenger booked with Air India to Jeddah is currently grounded until October 20, while an IndiGo passenger to Riyadh faces a cancellation window running to October 24.

ICAO Condemns Attacks on Civilian Airports

The latest extension came as the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Council strongly condemned the attacks on civilian airports, aircraft and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, expressing solidarity with the kingdom's government and people. The council's statement, issued on Thursday following a presentation by Saudi Arabia to the council on October 8, deplored the targeting of civil aviation infrastructure and the threat such attacks pose to aviation safety and international peace and security.

https://x.com/airindia/status/2110969241327546566

The human cost of the campaign is still rising. The death toll from the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has risen to 13, after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed the death of an Indian national who had been injured in the incident. The Houthis have also issued a broad warning to international airlines, foreign workers and commercial travellers to avoid Saudi aviation hubs, declaring Saudi airspace unsafe, with an explicit exception for the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

What This Means for Travellers

Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world, and the Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah routes carry heavy traffic from workers, families and Umrah pilgrims. We reported earlier this week that Indian airlines had cancelled Saudi flights through October 17 as the Riyadh airport closure was extended, and that India has opened 24-hour help for pilgrims caught in the disruption. Friday's announcements push the disruption at least three days further for Air India passengers and a full week further for IndiGo's.

Passengers with bookings in the cancellation windows should not travel to the airport. Air India is offering full refunds, and travellers should use the refund or rebooking options in their booking rather than buying a replacement ticket on the same route while suspensions are still being extended in stages.

What Happens Next

Each airline has tied resumption to the security situation rather than a fixed reopening of Saudi airspace, and the pattern of the past week — an October 17 deadline replaced by October 20, 21 and 24 deadlines within days — suggests further extensions remain possible if attacks on Saudi aviation infrastructure continue. Air India said it would continue monitoring developments and assess the situation before resuming operations.
